title: etcd / Raft — protocol internals
description: Explanation layer for etcd cells (metrics listener :2381, standard etcd 3.4 names — live-verified at M5.2). The harness CSVs are the result; this explains WHY.

panels.title: How to read an etcd run

options.content:
**Baseline expectation (corpus anchors: Raft paper / 'Raft Refloated' / Paxi's etcd runs):** exactly one member with `has_leader`=1 view across all members and ZERO leader changes for the whole window; proposals-committed rate ≈ the offered rate; proposals FAILED ≈ 0; WAL fsync p99 in the low-ms band on ccx13 NVMe — fsync IS etcd's per-commit durability cost, the structural difference vs in-memory Paxi (D6).

**leader_kill:** leader-change counter steps +1 within seconds of `fault_injected_at_ms`; committed-rate gap of well under a second (compare `failover_ms` in the manifest — Raft's sub-second re-election is the contrast anchor for the Paxi wedge). **A leader_kill with NO counter step = you killed a follower** (gate 3 reclassifies).

**Suspect signs:** proposals_pending climbing while committed-rate falls = quorum stress (check which member is gone); fsync p99 jumping ×10 = disk contention on that VM (environment, not protocol — note and rerun); has_leader flapping with no fault = real instability, stop and investigate.

panels.title: has_leader per member (1 = this member sees a leader)
Leader changes seen (gate-3 corroboration for leader_kill)
Proposals committed /s (should track the offered rate)
Proposals pending & failed (pending climbs = quorum stress; failed > 0 = investigate)
WAL fsync p99 (the durability cost Paxi does not pay — D6)
Member CPU busy (single-leader protocols: expect the leader's line on top — F8)
